After its premiere, prosecutors started complaining about the “CSI effect”—jurors demanding scientific evidence like DNA analysis in trials when none was available or appropriate. A 2008 survey of more than 2,000 jurors found that they were, in fact, increasingly more likely to expect lab-grade evidence from the state, but that the phenomenon wasn’t linked to their TV viewing habits. Instead, it seems like the jurors were generally more aware of scientific advancements in the field of forensics. But how scientific really are they? Sara Gordon, a law professor from the University of British Columbia, recently published a trio of deep dives into a few common techniques—which often go unquestioned by judges—and found them quite lacking.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
